docs.title: Python Udemy Tutorial
docs.text: Welcome to the Python Udemy Tutorial documentation. This project contains learning notes and code examples for Python fundamentals.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This tutorial covers the fundamental concepts of Python programming, organized into sections that build upon each other.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
To view this documentation locally, install MkDocs and run the development server:

pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser.

docs.title: Section One: Python Fundamentals
docs.text: Covers the basics of Python programming including: - Introduction to Python syntax - Variables and constants - Classes and objects - Array implementation

docs.title: Building Documentation
docs.text:
To build static HTML files:

mkdocs build

The generated site will be in the site/ directory.

docs.title: Variables and Constants
docs.text: This lesson covers variables and constants in Python, including declaration, assignment, and naming conventions.

docs.title: Concepts Covered
docs.text:
• Variable declaration and assignment
  • Constants and naming conventions
  • Variable reassignment
  • Multiple variable declarations
  • Assigning the same value to multiple variables

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variables are mutable objects that can be assigned different values. In Python, variables are created when you assign a value to them.

docs.title: Basic Variables
docs.text:
kount = 100
emp_name = "Robin"
age1, age2, age3 = 44, 27, 32

docs.title: Constants
docs.text:
Constants are immutable objects that should not be changed. Python uses naming conventions to identify constants (typically UPPERCASE).

PI = 3.14
GRAVITY = 9.8

docs.title: Variable Reassignment
docs.text:
Variables can be reassigned to different values, even different types:

a = "Apple"
a = "Aeroplane"
a = 100

docs.title: Multiple Variable Assignment
docs.text:
Python supports multiple variable declarations in a single line:

b, c, d = 1, 2.5, "Hello"

You can also assign the same value to multiple variables:

b = c = d = 5

docs.title: Running the Code
docs.text: python ./section-one/2variables-and-constants.py

docs.title: Classes and Objects
docs.text: Introduction to object-oriented programming in Python.

docs.title: Concepts Covered
docs.text:
• Class definition
  • Constructors and initialization
  • Class attributes
  • Methods
  • Object instantiation
  • Attribute modification
  • Object deletion

docs.title: Class Definition
docs.text:
A class is a blueprint for creating objects. It defines attributes and methods that the objects will have.

class MyComplexNumber:
    def __init__(self, real = 0, image = 0):
        self.real_part = real
        self.image_part = image

    def displayComplex(self):
        print("{0} + {1}j".format(self.real_part, self.image_part))

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text: The __init__ method is the constructor that initializes a new instance of the class. The self parameter refers to the instance being created.

docs.title: Creating Objects
docs.text:
Objects are created by calling the class name with arguments:

numberClass1 = MyComplexNumber(40, 50)
numberClass1.displayComplex()

docs.title: Modifying Attributes
docs.text:
You can modify object attributes after creation:

numberClass1.image_part += 10

You can also add new attributes dynamically:

numberClass2.new_attribute = 80

docs.title: Deleting Objects
docs.text:
Objects and their attributes can be deleted using the del statement:

del numberClass1.real_part  # Delete an attribute
del numberClass1            # Delete the entire object

docs.title: Running the Code
docs.text: python ./section-one/3python-class-and-objects.py

docs.title: Array Implementation
docs.text: Comprehensive guide to working with arrays (lists) in Python.

docs.title: Concepts Covered
docs.text:
• Array creation and indexing
  • Positive and negative indexing
  • Array operations (append, remove, pop)
  • Modifying array elements
  • Array concatenation
  • Repeating elements
  • Array slicing
  • Multi-dimensional arrays

docs.title: Creating Arrays
docs.text:
Arrays in Python are called lists. They can contain any type of data:

arr = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
brands = ["Coke", "Apple", "Google", "Microsoft", "Toyota"]

docs.title: Positive Indexing
docs.text:
Access elements from the beginning (0-based):

arr[0]  # First element: 10
arr[1]  # Second element: 20

docs.title: Negative Indexing
docs.text:
Access elements from the end:

arr[-1]  # Last element: 50
arr[-2]  # Second to last: 40

docs.title: Adding Elements
docs.text: brands.append("Intel")  # Adds to the end

docs.title: Removing Elements
docs.text:
del colors[4]              # Delete by index
colors.remove("blue")      # Delete by value
colors.pop(3)              # Delete by index and return value

docs.title: Modifying Elements
docs.text:
fruits[1] = "Pineapple"   # Modify by index
fruits[-1] = "Guava"       # Modify using negative index

docs.title: Array Concatenation
docs.text:
concat = [1, 2, 3]
concat = concat + [4, 5, 6]  # Result: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

docs.title: Repeating Elements
docs.text: repeat = ["a"] * 5  # Result: ['a', 'a', 'a', 'a', 'a']

docs.title: Array Slicing
docs.text:
Extract portions of an array:

fruits = ["Apple", "Banana", "Mango", "Grapes", "Orange"]
fruits[1:4]    # ['Banana', 'Mango', 'Grapes']
fruits[:3]     # ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Mango']
fruits[-4:]    # ['Banana', 'Mango', 'Grapes', 'Orange']
fruits[-3:-1]  # ['Mango', 'Grapes']

docs.title: Multi-dimensional Arrays
docs.text:
Arrays can contain other arrays:

multd = [[1,2], [3,4], [5,6], [7,8]]
multd[0]      # [1, 2]
multd[2][1]   # 6 (accessing nested element)

docs.title: Running the Code
docs.text: python ./section-one/4python-array-implementation.py
